chunks: Abu Abdillah Al-Ash'ari, from one of our companions, from Ja'far ibn Anbasa, from Ubada ibn Ziyad, from Amr ibn Abi Al-Miqdam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him); and Ahmad ibn Muhammad Al-Asimi, from the one who narrated to him, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said in his letter to Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Beware of consulting women, for their opinion leads to annihilation and their determination leads to weakness. Restrain their gaze from you by veiling them, for strict veiling is better for you and for them than doubt. And their going out is not more difficult than the entry of one whom you do not trust regarding them. So if you can ensure that no man other than you knows them, then do so.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad Al-Husayni, from Ali ibn Abdak, from Al-Hasan ibn Zarif ibn Nasih, from Al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Sa'd ibn Tareef, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), similar to it, except that he said: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) wrote this letter to his son Muhammad [ibn Al-Hanafiyya].'
ai.seo_question: What advice did Imam Ali give regarding the consultation of women and their veiling?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through multiple chains in Al-Kafi, records Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) epistle to his son Hasan (or Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah) regarding the management of women's social spheres. It highlights the Shia scholarly view on the psychological disposition of women, advising caution in consultation due to a tendency towards indecision, while prescribing strict hijab as a protective measure against social doubt (al-irtiyab). The emphasis on seclusion reflects the broader jurisprudential principle of safeguarding family honor and ensuring clear social boundaries.

en.hubeali: Abu Abdullah Al Ashary, from one of our companions, from Ja’far Bin Anbasa, from Ubada Bin Ziyad, from Amro Bin Abu Al Miqdam, from Abu Ja’farasws; and Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Aasimy, from the one who narrated it, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Abdul Rahman Bin Kaseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said regarding hisasws letter to Al-Hassanasws: ‘Beware of consulting the women, for their opinion leads to the annihilation, and their determination leads to the weakness, and restrain yourself from their gaze by your veiling from them, for the intense veiling is better for you and for them than the doubts, and their exit (from the house) is not more difficult than the entry of the one whom they cannot be relied upon to be with. So if you are able that no one other than you from the men can know them, so do it’.

Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Saeed, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Husayni, from Ali Bin Abdak, from Al Hassan Bin Zareyf Bin Nasih, from Al Husayn Bin Ulwan, from Sa’ad Bin Tareyf, from Al Asbagh Bin Nubata, 
from Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, similar to it, except that he said that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> wrote this letter to his<sup>asws</sup> son Muhammad (Bin Al-Hanafiyya)’.
en.sarwar: 7. Abu ‘Abd Allah al-Ash’ariy has narrated from certain persons of our people from Ja’far ibn ‘Anbasah from ‘Ubadah ibn Ziyad from ‘Amr ibn abu al-Miqdam from abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-‘Asemiy from those who narrated to him from al-‘Ala’ from Ali ibn Hassan from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Kathir who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, in his letter to al- Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam : ‘You must never consult women because their opinion is weak in reason and their aim is not durable. They must keep their eye cast down by means of your barrier, because strict privacy is better for you and for them and away from doubts. Their going out is not more difficult than entering of one to their place whom you do not trust about them. If you can, do something that no man other than you can know them; then do so.’”

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Sa‘id from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Husayniy from Ali ibn ‘Abdakin from al-Hassan ibn Tarif ibn Nasih from al-Husayn ibn ‘Ulwan from Sa‘d ibn Tarif from al- Asbagh ibn Nubatah from ‘Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a similar Hadith except that he has said ‘Amir al-Mu’minin wrote it to his son Muhammad (bin al-Hanafiyah).
